extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (requesters and patent owners), registered attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners/staff processing ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte reexamination filing and processing
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements and office practices for filing, prosecuting, and administratively handling ex parte reexamination requests and proceedings before the USPTO (MPEP guidance). Covers correspondence, filing date rules, amendments, fees, public access, record systems, event reporting, and examiner assignment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper addressing of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for ex parte reexamination and all subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence mailed via U.S. Postal Service and other correspondence to Office of the General Counsel pursuant to 37 CFR 1.1(a)(3) and 1.302(e) should be addressed: Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam, Attn: Central Reexamination Unit, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Hand-carried or commercial delivery should be addressed to the Customer Service Window with “Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam” included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether mailed, delivered, or hand-carried, it is strongly recommended that the Mail Stop information be placed in a prominent position on the first page of each paper using a sufficiently large font to direct attention to it. Use of the Customer Service Window for delivery service items (e.g., FedEx, DHL) is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fax prohibition for initial requests and corrected/replacement requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination may not be sent by facsimile transmission (FAX). This prohibition also applies to a corrected/completed request sent in response to a notice that the original request was not filing-date-compliant, since the corrected/completed request stands in place of, or is a completion of, the original request papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence, however, may be faxed to: Central Reexamination Unit (571) 273-9900.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing permitted for requests and follow-on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 9, 2007, the USPTO began accepting requests for reexamination and “follow-on” papers (reexamination subsequent correspondence proceedings) submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office updated the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System to permit such filings; see the Legal Framework and Patent Center guidance on www.uspto.gov/PatentLegalFramework for current procedures and permitted document types (see MPEP § 2267 for follow-on papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of reexamination proceeding on correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of the request for reexamination, any letters sent to the USPTO relating to the resulting ex parte reexamination proceeding should identify the proceeding by the number of the patent undergoing reexamination, the reexamination request control number assigned, the art unit, and the name of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including these identifiers ensures prompt routing and proper association with the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of mailing/transmission and Priority Mail Express
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) may be used to file any paper in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, except for a request for reexamination and a corrected/replacement request for reexamination. The Priority Mail Express® mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file any paper in an ex parte reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes filing of a patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and a requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.535. See MPEP §§ 512 and 513 for further guidance on using these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence directed to patent owner correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from the USPTO to the patent owner will be directed to the correspondence address for the patent being reexamined (see 37 CFR 1.33(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no correspondence address is otherwise specified, correspondence will be with the most recent attorney or agent made of record by the patent owner. Double correspondence with both owner and attorney/agent normally will not be undertaken by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owners, or the registered attorney or agent of record in the patent file, or any registered attorney or agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2213 for further details on signature requirements and acceptable signatories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on papers directed to merits prior to decision on request (untimely papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request under 35 U.S.C. 302, no papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than (A) citations of patents or printed publications under 37 CFR 1.501 or 1.555, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915, or (C) notifications pursuant to MPEP § 2282, should be filed with the Office prior to the date of the decision on the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other papers directed to the merits filed prior to the decision will be returned to the sender or expunged from the record if entered prior to discovery of the impropriety; a copy of the letter notifying of return/expungement will be made of record, but no copy of the returned/expunged papers will be retained by the Office. Such submissions may be filed later in the proceedings if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete request handling and opportunity to cure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not include the required fee and meet all requirements, the person identified as requesting reexamination will be notified and generally given an opportunity (generally 30 days) to complete the request. Failure to comply will result in the request not being granted a filing date and may result in placement of the request in the patent file as a citation if it complies with § 1.501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date of the request is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements of the section (37 CFR 1.510). Preprocessing includes forms (e.g., PTOL-2077 Notice of Failure to Comply; PTOL-2057 for fee deficiency; PTOL-2079 Preprocessing of Ex Parte Reexamination Request) to identify defects and guide remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure when request fails to comply prior to assigning a filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CRU LIE/Paralegal determine the request fails to meet filing-date requirements, the requester will be notified using form PTOL-2077 and given time to remedy defects; the notice will explain non-compliance items and may include attachments identifying the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not remedied within the specified time, the request will not be granted a filing date. If explanation is needed regarding a non-compliance item, the form’s box is checked and an attachment completed. Fee deficiencies are handled with PTOL-2057 attached to PTOL-2077.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to remedy defects after notice (including Decision Vacating Filing Date)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester does not timely respond to a notice of failure to comply, or responds but does not cure the defects or introduces new defects, the request papers will not be given a filing date (though a control number may be retained) and the Office may issue a Decision Vacating Filing Date or Decision Vacating the Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a filing date was previously assigned and non-compliance is later discovered, the examiner will communicate defects to CRU SPRS and OPLA; OPLA may issue a decision vacating the assigned filing date and give the requester one opportunity (absent extraordinary circumstances) to correct. Failure to remedy will result in termination of the proceeding; disposition of request papers (treated as §1.501 submission or discarded) will be explained in the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of filing of all complete reexamination requests filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 will be published in the Official Gazette approximately 4–5 weeks after filing. Both requests assigned a filing date and Director-initiated orders to reexamine will be announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice will be prepared by CRU reexamination preprocessing staff and forwarded to Office of Data Management for printing. The notice will appear under Requests for Ex Parte Reexamination Filed and will include the name of any requestor along with other items set forth in 37 CFR 1.11(c). Office personnel may use the Patent Data Portal to check whether a request has been filed for a particular patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice to patent owner via Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to deliver mail to the patent owner because no current address is available and all efforts fail, publication in the Official Gazette of the notice of filing of a request under 35 U.S.C. 302 or the notice of ordering of reexamination at the initiative of the Director will serve as constructive notice to the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeding will proceed without actual notice to the patent owner in such instances; publication timing and content follow MPEP § 2229 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of request corrections centralized in CRU
rubrics_metrics.description: All processing of submissions to cure an incomplete request for ex parte reexamination filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 is carried out by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU). Such submissions should be marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' so they may be promptly forwarded to CRU staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Mail Stop marking as discussed in MPEP § 2224; CRU handles preprocessing and clerical processing of corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files via Patent Center and certified copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public via Patent Center on the USPTO Internet site. Viewing images of proceedings allows access to entire content of the reexamination file with the exception of non-patent literature. Certified copies including non-patent literature may be ordered from PTCFB and orders should indicate the reexamination control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred that orders for certified copies be made through the PTCFB Certified Copy Center storefront (URL provided); alternatively orders may be mailed or emailed to dsd@uspto.gov and charges may be to credit card or deposit account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees applicable to ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under reexamination pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 302, fees are required for the request, for addition of claims (excess claims fees), for extension of time, and for any appeal, appeal forwarding fee, and oral hearing fees under 37 CFR 41.20(b). No fee is required for issue of the reexamination certificate. Petitions relating to a reexamination proceeding also require fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity-status reductions: micro entity reductions are available to patent owners only; small entity and micro entity reductions available to patent owner for excess claim, appeal, appeal forwarding, and oral hearing fees. For request and petition fees, small entity reductions are available to both third-party requesters and patent owners; micro entity reductions available only to patent owners. In merged proceedings only a single fee is needed even though multiple file submissions may be required. Expect about a 10-day lag between filing and database data entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal form and mailing practices for forwarding Office actions to requester
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal form with the requester’s address will be used to forward copies of Office actions (and any references cited in the Office actions) to the requester. A copy of this form will be made and attached to a copy of the Office action. When the patent owner is the requester, no such form is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice removes the need to retype the requester’s address each time a mailing is required and ensures accurate mailings to requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.121 for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530, and 37 CFR 1.121 (manner of making amendments in applications) applies, with specific reexamination provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendments may accompany a request filed by the patent owner (§1.510(e)), be part of a patent owner statement (§1.530(b)), or be filed during prosecution where permitted (§1.550(a) or §1.937). See MPEP § 2250 for manner of making amendments by patent owner and examples of proper claim amendment format; for clerical handling see MPEP § 2270.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for changes to specification other than claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification (other than claims, Large Tables §1.58(c), Computer Program Listing Appendix §1.96(c), Sequence Listing §1.821(c), or Sequence Listing XML §1.831(a)) must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph, including markings per paragraph (f), except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of the paragraph text. The precise point where any added or rewritten paragraph is located must be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to Large Tables, Computer Program Listing Appendix, Sequence Listing, or Sequence Listing XML must follow their respective rules (§1.58(g), §1.96(c)(5), §1.825, §1.835). All formal requirements for papers other than those set out in section are in §1.52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim proposed to be changed and of each new claim proposed to be added. For any claim changed, a parenthetical expression 'amended,' 'twice amended,' etc., should follow the claim number. Each changed or proposed added claim must include markings pursuant to paragraph (f), except that a patent claim or proposed added claim may be canceled by a statement canceling the claim without presentation of the claim text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claim text must be presented in full for any amendment; see MPEP §2250 for examples of proper claim amendment format. Claims may not be renumbered; added claims must follow the numbering of the highest-numbered patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for drawings changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval, only new sheets of drawings including the changes and in compliance with §1.84 must be filed. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures must be surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketches are for examiner approval; final submission must be new sheets in compliance with drawing rules. See §1.84 for format of drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes must be supplied
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims pursuant to paragraph (d), there must also be supplied, on pages separate from the pages containing the changes, the status (i.e., pending or canceled), as of the date of the amendment, of all patent claims and of all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separate statement demonstrates that claim changes are supported by the original disclosure and clarifies the claim set post-amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings to show changes (brackets and underlining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include the following markings: (1) matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; and (2) matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments must visibly show insertions and deletions with these markings; where a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate ALL changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text of the patent under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renumbering prohibition and numbering of added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims must not be renumbered. The numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest-numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves traceability of original claim numbering; see MPEP §2235 and related sections for clerical handling and entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of disclosure may be required to secure correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require changes to ensure consistency among claims, specification, and drawings; amendments must be relative to the patent specification and drawings in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be relative to patent as of filing date of request
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification, including the claims, and drawings, which are in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot base amendments on intervening changes; the baseline is the patent text in effect on the request filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope or introduction of new matter; restrictions for expired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Moreover, no amendment, other than the cancellation of claims, will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict substantive limitation: amendments are limited to narrowing or clarifying the claims without adding new subject matter or expanding scope; cancellations are permitted even after expiration, but additions/changes will not be incorporated post-expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendments not legally effective until reexamination certificate issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments entered for purposes of examination are not legally binding until the certificate issues; MPEP §2250 and §2235 discuss manner of making amendments and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record systems and retrieval of reexamination data on OPSG/Patent Data Portal
rubrics_metrics.description: The One Patent Service Gateway (OPSG) system is used to support the reexamination process. Routine OPSG retrieval transactions and Patent Data Portal/IFW displays allow Office staff to obtain reexamination data (e.g., search by patent number, continuity data to obtain reexamination number). Reexamination e-files may be viewed on IFW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some data entry for reexamination differs from regular patent applications; status codes for reexamination generally in the '400' range. If paper files exist, they should be ordered and scanned into IFW. File movement is monitored by File Ordering System (FOS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting major events to OPSG and permanent recording
rubrics_metrics.description: The OPSG system is used to monitor and report major events in processing reexamination proceedings (e.g., determination mailed—denial or grant, petitions received/decided, owner/requester responses received, mailing of examiner actions). These events will be permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of the application records and status displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU Technical Support Staff is responsible for reporting events; status representative of events will also be displayed. Examples of reportable events are enumerated in the MPEP text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status reports and management reports to assure 'special dispatch'
rubrics_metrics.description: Various automated reports generated from OPSG are available to CRU and appropriate TCs to indicate when deadlines are approaching and to assure reexaminations are processed with 'special dispatch.' Examples include lists of requests not assigned to an examiner by the sixth week since filing, proceedings awaiting first action after grant, reexaminations located in CRU with action type and date, and proceedings forwarded to PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports are used for monitoring workload and meeting processing timeliness; CRU and TC staff should consult them regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment policy for reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests are generally assigned to the CRU art unit where the patent is currently classified and assigned to a primary examiner other than the examiner who originally examined the patent. The CRU SPRS assigns to an examiner most familiar with the claimed subject matter, but normally not one who participated previously in examination of the patent or its parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy precludes assignment to an examiner who prepared/signed an action or participated as conferee in prior examination, except in rare cases where the original examiner is the only examiner with adequate knowledge of the technology. Such exceptions require CRU Director approval and must be stated in the decision or indicated by the Director’s signature on the order/action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and special assignment rules (copending reissue/reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions include: (A) if the original examiner is the only examiner with adequate knowledge, assignment to that examiner may be approved by CRU Director and noted; (B) if an earlier concluded reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner will generally be assigned the new reexamination; (C) when reissue and reexamination are copending or merger is considered, assignment rules depend on whether reexamination has been ordered and whether the examiner was involved in prior examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reissue is pending and a reexamination is filed, the request is generally assigned to an examiner who did not examine the original patent application; if merged, the merged proceeding will generally be handled by the examiner who would ordinarily handle the reissue application, subject to conflict rules. If reexamination has been ordered and merger is considered, OPLA should be notified promptly and files scanned into IFW if paper.
